name: The Heron
note: a grey heron — compact body on two stilt legs, one folded wing, a neck that keeps an S at rest and reaches out to strike. Root pivot is the shoulder where the neck leaves the body; faces +X. Legs and wing run down their length (+Y); neck, head and tail are drawn away from the body, so a positive angle tips a part forward. Held at the shoulder, under the jaw and at the wing; the legs are unheld.

parts.note: compact body, deepest at the breast and tapering up to the rump at [-24,3]; the back runs from the shoulder at [0,0], the belly hangs to y=16, the breast juts to x=12
short wedge tail, carried back and well down from the rump so its tip forks out just below the tip of the folded wing
lower neck, thickest of the three; leaves the shoulder leaning back and arches forward 45° — the bottom of the rest S
middle neck; turns back the other way 50°, cutting the notch in the front of the S. Its pivot sits on the tip of neck_low and its rounded base seals that joint at any bend
upper neck, the slenderest segment; curves forward again to carry the head back over the shoulders

skull barely deeper than the neck, its crown running straight out into a long dagger bill, tip at [35,0.8]; the crest plume sweeps back and down off the crown to a point at [-10.6,-0.2]. The hand rod attaches under the jaw at [6,1.8] and drives the whole neck from there down to the shoulder

the near wing, one blade folded along the back at rest — broad at the shoulder, tapering to a point past the tail — its tip is the rearmost thing on the bird. Rotating it at the shoulder past 90° lifts it open; the wire is out at [-0.6,28], near the tip
far leg, the feathered upper leg (tibia) — stick-thin, slanting back 25 down to the ankle
far lower leg (tarsus) — slants forward again, so the ankle above it reads as the backward-bending knee of a wading bird
far foot, a flat splayed blade — long forward toes and a short hind toe, level with the ground at rest
near leg, upper (tibia); stands a little more upright than the far one
